slides.claim: Can caesium incorporation remove the damp-heat failure route of a mixed-halide absorber?

notes.say: Frame the question, not the paper. The room knows phase segregation, so the opening has to define what a satisfactory answer would look like: a retention number, a mechanism-side measurement, and an explicit statement of what is still unknown.
notes.checkpoint: Question on screen before the first data slide

slides.claim: 1000 h of damp heat separates the two absorbers: 73.8 % retention for the reference, 96.2 % with Cs

notes.say: Lead with the contrast. Both groups started near 21 %, so the entire gap at 1000 h is a difference in degradation rate, not in the starting point. Do not explain the mechanism yet; let the number sit for a moment before moving on.

slides.claim: The Cs-incorporated absorber trades a little initial efficiency for damp-heat stability

notes.say: Quantify the trade. The reference loses about a quarter of its efficiency; the Cs-incorporated film loses almost nothing. Say explicitly that this is an encapsulated device result under lab cycling and that nothing here is a module-level claim.
notes.checkpoint: Trade-off stated as a rate difference

slides.claim: What moves with retention is the delta-phase fraction, not the starting efficiency

notes.say: This is the part of the story that was not settled before: the amount of photo-inactive delta phase tracks how much efficiency survives. When asked why phase fraction should be the read-out, point at the ordering rather than at the absolute values.

slides.claim: Two groups, 24 encapsulated devices each, cycled at 85 C and 85 % RH for 1000 h

notes.say: Keep this short and concrete: the room cares about the encapsulation stack and the sampling density, not about the spin-coating recipe. Mention that the same encapsulation and the same chamber were used for both groups, which is what makes the comparison meaningful.

slides.claim: After 1000 h the delta-phase fraction is 31.5 % in the reference film and 4.2 % with Cs

notes.say: Walk the audience across the plot once, left to right. The reference curve bends upward after roughly 500 h while the Cs-incorporated curve stays flat, so the divergence starts mid-experiment. Offer the raw rows as the checkable source, not just the plot.
notes.checkpoint: Plot read left to right once, no re-reading

slides.claim: Activation energy rises from 0.78 eV to 1.12 eV and T80 from 240 h to 1450 h

notes.say: Give the kinetic numbers as estimates, not constants: three temperatures is the minimum for a straight-line fit. If the room pushes, agree that the error bar is unknown and offer the raw data as the way to settle it later.

slides.claim: The claim is bounded by a 1000 h window, one encapsulation stack, 24 devices and three temperatures

notes.say: Say the limit before anyone asks for it. The honest sentence is that this shows a rate difference inside one stack, and that an extrapolated lifetime would need a longer window and more temperatures. Then stop talking.
notes.checkpoint: A limitation is stated by us, not extracted from us

slides.claim: Cs incorporation keeps the black phase and retains 96.2 % of initial PCE after 1000 h

notes.say: Close on the one sentence the room should remember, then hand over the open item. Do not re-read the agenda or re-list the slides; the conclusion is stronger when it is said once.
